1. **The problem: too much work inside the Jest runner.**

   This PR changes test execution infrastructure, rather than application behavior. Previously, Bazel launched one Jest process with `--runInBand`, using the standard `ts-jest` preset. The PR description identifies repeated TypeScript program construction as the dominant cost. See the original [Jest configuration](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/54e4e293dfe4e142bf8a63761f4f0348af205a0e/frontend/jest.config.cjs#L1-L8) and [Bazel target](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/54e4e293dfe4e142bf8a63761f4f0348af205a0e/frontend/BUILD#L38-L58).

   The solution removes type checking from Jest’s transform and distributes test files across four Bazel processes. The PR reports 58 suites and 449 tests partitioned across those shards. Its worker experiment measured **39.6–43.3 seconds with in-band shards**, versus **97.9–102.4 seconds with four Jest workers inside each shard**. Those measurements compare worker configurations; they do not independently establish the title’s 2.2× improvement over the base revision.

2. **The core implementation: transpile each file, then let Bazel own parallelism.**

   The preset becomes an explicit transform whose important settings are:

   ```js
   "^.+\\.[tj]sx?$": [
     "ts-jest",
     {
       isolatedModules: true,
       tsconfig: {
         module: "CommonJS",
         moduleResolution: "Node",
         esModuleInterop: true,
       },
     },
   ],
   ```

   `isolatedModules: true` makes this a transpile-only path. The module overrides adapt the application’s TypeScript configuration to Jest’s CommonJS runtime; other settings remain inherited. The changed contract is that **Jest no longer performs type checking**. The configuration comments and PR description say CI separately checks all of `src`, including tests. That CI configuration and the underlying TypeScript configuration were not supplied, so this review cannot independently verify that safeguard. [Transform and rationale](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.config.cjs#L9-L32)

   Bazel adds `shard_count = 4` while retaining `--runInBand`. Each shard still receives the discovered test paths; the new sequencer selects its share at runtime. Thus, parallel execution happens between Bazel shards, with serial Jest execution inside each one. [Bazel wiring](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/BUILD#L38-L64)

3. **The main logic to review is the translation from Bazel’s shard environment to a test-file partition.**

   The sequencer sorts files by descending size, breaking ties by path. It then assigns sorted positions round-robin:

   ```js
   const total = Number(process.env.TEST_TOTAL_SHARDS);
   const index = Number(process.env.TEST_SHARD_INDEX);
   const ordered = [...tests].sort(bySizeThenPath);
   if (!Number.isInteger(total) || total < 1 || !Number.isInteger(index)) {
     return ordered;
   }
   return ordered.filter((_, i) => i % total === index);
   ```

   File size is a cost heuristic, not a measured runtime. Files that cannot be statted receive size zero. The partition logic is the decisive step that makes four processes divide the work instead of repeat it. [Ordering and partitioning](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.shard-sequencer.cjs#L27-L52)

   **Worked example — illustrative inputs:** suppose eight discovered files, `a.test.ts` through `h.test.ts`, have descending sizes of 800, 700, …, 100 bytes.

   - **Before:** the unsharded Bazel target passes all eight files to one in-band Jest process. All eight execute there; their exact order depends on Jest’s default sequencer.
   - **After:** Bazel launches four shards with `TEST_TOTAL_SHARDS="4"` and indices `"0"` through `"3"`. Each sequencer sorts the files into `a` through `h`, then applies the modulo filter:

     | Shard index | Sorted positions retained | Files executed |
     |---|---|---|
     | 0 | 0, 4 | a, e |
     | 1 | 1, 5 | b, f |
     | 2 | 2, 6 | c, g |
     | 3 | 3, 7 | d, h |

   The observable result is eight file executions spread across four processes, with each file selected exactly once. This balances file counts and spreads larger files across shards; it does not guarantee equal execution times.

   Three supporting details complete the integration:

   - **Bazel handshake:** loading the sequencer writes an empty `TEST_SHARD_STATUS_FILE`, when provided, to advertise sharding support. The comments explain why the runtime environment is used instead of a fixed Jest `--shard` argument. [Protocol handling](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.shard-sequencer.cjs#L5-L25)
   - **Local behavior:** the custom sequencer is installed only when `TEST_TOTAL_SHARDS` is truthy. Ordinary local runs retain Jest’s default sequencer, although they also receive the new transpile-only transform. [Conditional configuration](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.config.cjs#L3-L9)
   - **Caching:** Bazel’s Jest cache moves to `${TEST_TMPDIR}/jest-cache`; without that variable, the default location remains. The custom sequencer’s `cacheResults()` does nothing, intentionally foregoing timing persistence in Bazel sandboxes. [Cache directory](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.config.cjs#L33-L34), [sequencer cache hook](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.shard-sequencer.cjs#L58-L60)

4. **The added test protects against partitioning failed tests twice.**

   The single new test sets four shards and index one, then supplies three nonexistent paths in order `c, a, b`. Because stat failures produce zero sizes, path ordering gives `a, b, c`. It verifies two distinct contracts:

   ```js
   sequencer.sort(tests)           // selects b
   sequencer.allFailedTests(tests) // retains a, b, c
   ```

   This is the useful boundary case: a failed-test list already belonging to a shard must retain every supplied entry. Reusing `sort()` there would retain only `b`, dropping `a` and `c`. Accordingly, `allFailedTests()` only orders its input; it does not apply the modulo filter. [Regression test](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/src/jest.shard-sequencer.test.js#L25-L39), [implementation](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.shard-sequencer.cjs#L54-L56)

   Infrastructure changes comprise the transform, conditional sequencer, four-way Bazel sharding, cache placement, and explicit inclusion of the `.cjs` sequencer in Bazel runfiles. The existing `jest.setup.cjs` registration remains in both Jest and Bazel. [Runfiles](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/BUILD#L47-L55), [setup registration](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.config.cjs#L8)

   The added unit test does **not** cover real file-size ordering, the complete cross-shard partition, or the status-file handshake. The PR reports successful Bazel build/test and `checkleft run`; I have reviewed the supplied pinned source, not rerun those checks.

# PR #1552: Faster Jest transforms and four Bazel-owned shards

## 1. Problem being solved

The frontend Jest target previously ran its full test list in one process using the `ts-jest` preset. The PR addresses two sources of elapsed time: TypeScript transformation overhead and serial execution of the suite. The author reports that profiling identified repeated TypeScript program construction as the dominant cost; the supplied source establishes the old configuration, but does not include those profiles. See the [base Jest configuration](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/54e4e293dfe4e142bf8a63761f4f0348af205a0e/frontend/jest.config.cjs#L1-L7) and [base Bazel target](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/54e4e293dfe4e142bf8a63761f4f0348af205a0e/frontend/BUILD#L38-L58).

This guide covers the complete comparison from `54e4e293` to `7db88ee2`. Links below pin the supplied source revisions; exact diff anchors were not provided.

## 2. Core fix / implementation

The change combines two independent optimizations:

- **Transpile files without Jest-side type checking.** An explicit `ts-jest` transform replaces the preset and enables `isolatedModules`.
- **Partition test files across four Bazel shards.** A custom sequencer reads Bazel’s runtime shard environment and selects each shard’s files. Each Jest process retains `--runInBand`, so Bazel controls parallelism.

The [transform configuration](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.config.cjs#L9-L31) contains the essential compiler settings:

```js
"^.+\\.[tj]sx?$": [
  "ts-jest",
  {
    isolatedModules: true,
    // ...
    tsconfig: {
      module: "CommonJS",
      moduleResolution: "Node",
      esModuleInterop: true,
    },
  },
],
```

The CommonJS overrides adapt the transform to Jest’s runtime. The surrounding comment says other compiler settings are inherited from the application configuration.

**Type checking is now a separate responsibility.** The PR description and configuration comment say CI runs `tsc` over all of `src`, including tests, under the same frontend-change condition. Neither that CI configuration nor the TypeScript configuration is supplied, so this retained coverage cannot be independently verified here. The Jest configuration itself does not enforce that a separate type-check runs.

## 3. Walkthrough of the implementation

### Start with the Bazel execution boundary

The [Bazel target](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/BUILD#L38-L64) still passes the globbed test paths with `--runTestsByPath` and retains `--runInBand`. It adds:

```python
"jest.shard-sequencer.cjs",  # in data
```

and:

```python
shard_count = 4,
```

Thus each shard receives the target’s test list; the sequencer performs the actual partition. Adding the `.cjs` file explicitly to runfiles matters because the existing JavaScript/TypeScript source glob does not include that extension.

### Activate the sequencer from runtime state

[Jest configuration](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.config.cjs#L3-L8) installs the custom sequencer conditionally:

```js
...(process.env.TEST_TOTAL_SHARDS
  ? { testSequencer: "<rootDir>/jest.shard-sequencer.cjs" }
  : {}),
```

The condition is a truthy environment value, not independent detection of Bazel. With that variable absent, bare Jest retains its default sequencer; the new transform still applies.

When the sequencer module loads, it [writes the shard-status file](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.shard-sequencer.cjs#L22-L25), if supplied:

```js
const statusFile = process.env.TEST_SHARD_STATUS_FILE;
if (statusFile) {
  fs.writeFileSync(statusFile, "");
}
```

This acknowledges sharding support. It happens before selection and is not validation of the shard parameters.

### Order once, then distribute by position

The [ordering helper](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.shard-sequencer.cjs#L27-L37) sorts larger files first, breaking size ties by path. Failed filesystem lookups count as size zero.

The [core partition](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.shard-sequencer.cjs#L44-L52) is:

```js
const total = Number(process.env.TEST_TOTAL_SHARDS);
const index = Number(process.env.TEST_SHARD_INDEX);
const ordered = [...tests].sort(bySizeThenPath);
if (!Number.isInteger(total) || total < 1 || !Number.isInteger(index)) {
  return ordered;
}
return ordered.filter((_, i) => i % total === index);
```

For four shards, shard zero receives positions `0, 4, 8…`; shard one receives `1, 5, 9…`. With identical ordering and valid indices, this partitions the list without overlap. File size is a cost heuristic, so equal runtime is not guaranteed.

Validation is limited: invalid totals or noninteger indices return the full ordered list, but integer indices outside `0…total-1` produce an empty selection.

### Worked example: selection and failed-test preservation

Use the [added test’s synthetic fixture](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/src/jest.shard-sequencer.test.js#L7-L10), with its [inputs and assertions](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/src/jest.shard-sequencer.test.js#L25-L38):

```text
TEST_TOTAL_SHARDS = "4"
TEST_SHARD_INDEX  = "1"
input paths: /missing/c.test.js, /missing/a.test.js, /missing/b.test.js
```

These are missing-file test objects, not executable suites.

1. **Before:** the Bazel target had no sharding, and Jest had no custom partition. There was no shard-selection step reducing the target’s test list; its default ordering is not established by the supplied code.
2. **After:** each size lookup fails and returns zero. Path ordering produces `[a, b, c]`.
3. Positions are `[0, 1, 2]`. Only position `1` satisfies `i % 4 === 1`, so `sort(tests)` returns **`[b]`**, exactly as asserted.
4. For the failed-test hook, the contract differs: an already-selected list must retain its membership. [`allFailedTests(tests)`](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.shard-sequencer.cjs#L54-L56) returns **`[a, b, c]`**. Reusing `sort()` there would incorrectly discard `a` and `c`.

The test directly proves those two method results. Jest’s caller is not supplied, so the statement that the failed-test hook receives an already-sharded list comes from the intended integration contract, rather than a traced caller. The method itself only orders its input; it does not identify failures.

### Keep temporary state scoped to Bazel

The [cache setting](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.config.cjs#L32-L34) uses `${TEST_TMPDIR}/jest-cache` when that variable is truthy; otherwise Jest chooses its default location. Separately, the custom sequencer’s [`cacheResults()` is empty](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.shard-sequencer.cjs#L58-L60), so it does not persist sequencing timings.

## 4. Tests and supporting infrastructure

**Added:** one regression test asserts that `sort()` partitions the fixture while `allFailedTests()` preserves all three entries in sorted order. It sets shard variables before the test and restores their original values afterward. Missing paths exercise the zero-size fallback without creating fixture files. See the [complete test](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/src/jest.shard-sequencer.test.js#L1-L40).

**Modified or removed tests:** none in the supplied comparison.

**Infrastructure changes:** the existing Bazel glob automatically includes the new `.test.js` file; runfiles gain the sequencer; the target gains four shards; Jest gains the explicit transform, conditional sequencer, and temporary-directory cache. The existing `jest.setup.cjs` configuration and runfile entry remain present. Its claimed TextEncoder/TextDecoder polyfill is not supplied for inspection.

The regression does **not** directly test real-file size balancing, complete cross-shard coverage, status-file acknowledgement, or the separate CI type-check. Those remain distinct from the behavior its assertions establish.

The author reports successful `bazel build`, `bazel test`, and `checkleft run`, plus 58 suites and 449 tests partitioned across four shards. Reported in-band timings were 39.6–43.3 seconds versus 97.9–102.4 seconds with four Jest workers inside each shard, supporting the retained `--runInBand` choice. That comparison does not independently establish the title’s 2.2× improvement over the base revision. No tests or benchmarks were run for this guide.

# PR #1552: Faster Jest transforms and Bazel-owned sharding

This guide covers base `54e4e293dfe4e142bf8a63761f4f0348af205a0e` → head `7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1`. Links below use pinned source locations because exact diff anchors were not supplied.

## 1. Problem being solved

The frontend’s Bazel Jest target previously ran every test file in one process using the default `ts-jest` preset. The author reports that profiling identified repeated TypeScript program construction as the dominant cost. Meanwhile, CI already ran a separate TypeScript build, so Jest’s semantic checking duplicated work.

The PR addresses both transformation cost and execution parallelism. Its title reports a **2.2× speedup**; that is an author-reported measurement, not a result independently reproduced for this guide.

## 2. Core fix / implementation

The solution separates three responsibilities:

- **Jest transpiles and executes tests.** An explicit `ts-jest` transform enables file-by-file compilation without semantic type-checking.
- **The existing frontend build checks TypeScript.** CI schedules this build under the same condition as the Bazel frontend tests.
- **Bazel partitions execution into four shards.** A new Jest sequencer translates Bazel’s runtime environment into disjoint file selections. Each shard retains `--runInBand`, avoiding another layer of Jest workers.

The transform change applies to local Jest runs too. The custom sequencer applies only when `TEST_TOTAL_SHARDS` is truthy. Running Jest or the Bazel test target alone therefore no longer provides the semantic checking supplied by the separate frontend build. See the [Jest configuration](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.config.cjs#L3-L33) and [Bazel target](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/BUILD#L38-L64).

## 3. Walkthrough of the implementation

### First, remove type-checking from the transform

The former `preset: "ts-jest"` becomes an explicit transform. Its decisive options are:

```js
isolatedModules: true,
tsconfig: {
  module: "CommonJS",
  moduleResolution: "Node",
  esModuleInterop: true,
},
```

The outer `isolatedModules` option selects ts-jest’s transpile-only path. That is distinct from the pre-existing TypeScript `isolatedModules` compiler option, which constrains source compatibility with file-by-file compilation. The module overrides adapt the application’s ESM/bundler configuration to Jest’s CommonJS execution; JSX, Emotion’s JSX import source, and other compiler settings remain inherited. See [transform options](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.config.cjs#L17-L30) and [TypeScript configuration](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/tsconfig.json#L2-L25).

The replacement type-checking path is concrete: [CI schedules both frontend steps together](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/.buildkite/scripts/upload_dynamic_pipeline.sh#L146-L159); the [npm step runs `npm run build`](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/.buildkite/scripts/run_frontend_tests.sh#L9-L13); and that [build starts with `tsc`](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/package.json#L6-L10). The tsconfig includes `src`, including its TypeScript tests. This does not mean the newly added JavaScript test receives TypeScript checking: `allowJs`/`checkJs` are not enabled.

### Next, make each Bazel invocation select its own files

The [BUILD change](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/BUILD#L38-L64) adds `shard_count = 4` and includes the `.cjs` sequencer in runfiles. The existing test-file glob and `--runTestsByPath` arguments still supply the full candidate list to each invocation.

The sequencer then:

1. Writes an empty `TEST_SHARD_STATUS_FILE`, when supplied, to acknowledge sharding support.
2. Sorts a copy of the candidates by descending file size, breaking ties with `path.localeCompare`.
3. Selects positions belonging to the current zero-based shard.

The [selection logic](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.shard-sequencer.cjs#L44-L51) is:

```js
const total = Number(process.env.TEST_TOTAL_SHARDS);
const index = Number(process.env.TEST_SHARD_INDEX);
const ordered = [...tests].sort(bySizeThenPath);
if (!Number.isInteger(total) || total < 1 || !Number.isInteger(index)) {
  return ordered;
}
return ordered.filter((_, i) => i % total === index);
```

File size is a cost heuristic, not a guarantee of equal runtime. A failed file-stat operation contributes size zero. The guard also assumes Bazel supplies a valid index range: integer indices outside `0..total-1` yield no selected files. See the [status handshake and comparator](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.shard-sequencer.cjs#L21-L36).

### Worked example: one candidate list, four executions

**Illustrative inputs:** eight valid TypeScript test files, `a.test.ts` through `h.test.ts`, with strictly descending sizes of 8 KB through 1 KB. Each shard sees the same files and metadata; Bazel supplies `TEST_TOTAL_SHARDS="4"` and indices `"0"` through `"3"`.

**Before:** the [base target](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/54e4e293dfe4e142bf8a63761f4f0348af205a0e/frontend/BUILD#L38-L58) has no shard count. One in-band Jest invocation runs all eight files through the default ts-jest configuration.

**After:** every invocation computes the order `a,b,c,d,e,f,g,h`, then applies the modulo selection above:

| Shard index | Selected positions | Files executed |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0, 4 | a, e |
| 1 | 1, 5 | b, f |
| 2 | 2, 6 | c, g |
| 3 | 3, 7 | d, h |

For shard 1, `b` survives because `1 % 4 === 1`; `f` survives because `5 % 4 === 1`. The other six candidates are excluded from that invocation.

**Observable result:** the four invocations collectively execute every test file once, two files per process, with transpile-only transforms. They can run concurrently as Bazel resources permit. Shared imported modules may still be transformed in multiple shards; the change does not promise globally unique compilation or equal shard durations.

### Finally, avoid partitioning again and control cache lifetime

The sequencer deliberately gives failed-test selection a separate implementation:

```js
allFailedTests(tests) {
  return [...tests].sort(bySizeThenPath);
}
```

[Jest 29.7 calls `sort` before its `onlyFailures` handling](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jestjs/jest/v29.7.0/packages/jest-core/src/runJest.ts). Calling the partitioning `sort` again could discard files already assigned to this shard. The [new hook](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.shard-sequencer.cjs#L54-L60) preserves all incoming candidates and only orders them. Despite its name, it does **not** determine which candidates previously failed; `cacheResults()` is also a no-op.

Separately, [Jest’s cache directory](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.config.cjs#L33) becomes `${TEST_TMPDIR}/jest-cache` when that variable is truthy. Without these environment overrides, local runs retain Jest’s default sequencer and cache location.

## 4. Tests and supporting infrastructure

**Added:** one [regression test](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/src/jest.shard-sequencer.test.js#L25-L39), with two complementary assertions. It sets total shards to four and index to one, then supplies nonexistent paths in `c,a,b` order:

```js
expect(sequencer.sort(tests).map((test) => test.path))
  .toEqual(["/missing/b.test.js"]);
```

All stat calls fall back to zero, so the path tie-break produces `a,b,c`; partitioning keeps only `b`. Calling `allFailedTests` on the same three candidates must instead return all three in `a,b,c` order. The fixture is entirely synthetic—no files are created—and teardown restores or removes the original environment variables.

**Modified or removed tests:** none. The complete comparison changes two configuration/build files and adds the sequencer plus this test.

**Supporting infrastructure:** the existing BUILD glob automatically discovers the new `.test.js`; the new `.cjs` helper is explicitly added to runfiles. The pre-existing jsdom setup and its [TextEncoder/TextDecoder polyfill](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.setup.cjs#L1-L11) remain wired into both Jest and Bazel.

**Coverage limits:** the unit test verifies partition-versus-order behavior directly. It does not exercise real size-based balancing, the status-file handshake, the full Jest failed-test lifecycle, or complete four-shard coverage.

**Validation:** the author reports successful `bazel build //frontend:jest_test`, `bazel test //frontend:jest_test --test_output=errors`, and `checkleft run`, with 58 suites and 449 tests partitioned across four shards. Reported in-band timings were 39.6–43.3 seconds versus 97.9–102.4 seconds with four Jest workers inside each shard. For this guide, the pinned comparison, CI/type-checking path, and Jest caller behavior were inspected; tests and benchmarks were not rerun.

# PR #1552: Faster Jest execution through transpilation and Bazel sharding

## 1. Problem being solved

This guide covers the complete comparison from `54e4e293` to `7db88ee2`. Links below pin source to those revisions.

The frontend’s Bazel test target previously ran the entire Jest suite in one process using the default `ts-jest` preset. The PR reports that repeated TypeScript program construction dominated runtime. It addresses that compilation overhead and adds parallel execution across test files.

The reported performance measurements are author results, not independently reproduced here: four in-band Bazel shards completed in **39.6–43.3 seconds**, compared with **97.9–102.4 seconds** when each shard also used four Jest workers. That comparison supports retaining one Jest process per shard; it does not independently establish the title’s overall **2.2×** improvement against the base revision.

## 2. Core fix / implementation

The change separates three responsibilities:

- **Jest transpiles and executes tests.** An explicit `ts-jest` transform replaces the preset and enables transpile-only operation.
- **Bazel schedules parallel work.** The target requests four shards while retaining `--runInBand`.
- **The existing frontend build checks TypeScript.** CI schedules that build alongside the Bazel tests.

The new sequencer connects Bazel’s runtime shard environment to Jest’s test selection. Each shard receives the full candidate file list, sorts it consistently, and keeps its own round-robin subset. Adding `shard_count` alone would not implement that selection.

The shared Jest configuration also places its cache under `TEST_TMPDIR` when that variable is set. Without the relevant environment variables, local Jest keeps its default sequencer and cache location—but still uses the new transpile-only transform. See [Jest configuration](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.config.cjs#L2-L34) and [Bazel target](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/BUILD#L37-L64).

## 3. Implementation walkthrough and worked example

### Remove type-checking work from Jest

The decisive transform options are:

```js
isolatedModules: true,
tsconfig: {
  module: "CommonJS",
  moduleResolution: "Node",
  esModuleInterop: true,
},
```

These options select file-by-file transpilation and adapt the app’s ESM/bundler configuration to Jest’s CommonJS runtime. Other settings—including the Emotion JSX configuration—remain inherited from the application tsconfig. The transform pattern now matches JS/JSX as well as TS/TSX. See [the transform](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.config.cjs#L9-L32) and [inherited compiler options](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/tsconfig.json#L2-L25).

The replacement type-checking path is verifiable: the dynamic pipeline emits both frontend steps under the same `need_frontend` condition; the npm step runs `npm run build`; that script starts with `tsc`; and tsconfig includes `src` without excluding TypeScript tests. This supports the comment’s claim for TS/TSX tests in `src`. It does **not** make a standalone Bazel Jest invocation a type check, nor enable JavaScript checking for the newly added `.js` test. See [CI scheduling](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/.buildkite/scripts/upload_dynamic_pipeline.sh#L146-L159), [CI commands](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/.buildkite/scripts/run_frontend_tests.sh#L9-L13), and [build script](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/package.json#L6-L11).

### Partition files when Bazel launches each shard

The [Bazel target](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/BUILD#L37-L64) retains explicit test paths and `--runInBand`, adds the sequencer to runfiles, and sets `shard_count = 4`. Bazel can schedule four actions; Jest does not create another worker pool within each action.

The configuration installs the custom sequencer when `TEST_TOTAL_SHARDS` is truthy. On module load, the sequencer writes an empty `TEST_SHARD_STATUS_FILE`, if supplied, to acknowledge sharding support. Its core selection is:

```js
const ordered = [...tests].sort(bySizeThenPath);
if (!Number.isInteger(total) || total < 1 || !Number.isInteger(index)) {
  return ordered;
}
return ordered.filter((_, i) => i % total === index);
```

The comparator orders files by descending byte size, breaking ties with `path.localeCompare`. Failed file stats count as size zero. This distributes file counts evenly for valid shard indices, assuming every shard sees the same files and ordering; file size is only a runtime-cost heuristic. See [ordering and selection](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.shard-sequencer.cjs#L22-L52).

The guard is limited: it checks integer values and a positive total, but does not enforce `0 <= index < total`. Correct index bounds come from the expected Bazel environment.

### Worked example: distributing one candidate list

**Illustrative input**, applying the implemented algorithm: five test files have sizes `a=500`, `b=400`, `c=300`, `d=200`, and `e=100` bytes. Discovery returns them in any order.

At the [base revision](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/54e4e293dfe4e142bf8a63761f4f0348af205a0e/frontend/BUILD#L37-L58), one in-band Jest invocation runs all five files. Its execution order may depend on Jest’s default sequencer, but no Bazel partition removes any of them.

At the head revision, each action receives `TEST_TOTAL_SHARDS="4"` and its own zero-based `TEST_SHARD_INDEX`:

1. Sorting produces `[a, b, c, d, e]`.
2. Their positions modulo four are `[0, 1, 2, 3, 0]`.
3. The actions select:

| Shard index | Files executed |
|---|---|
| 0 | `a`, `e` |
| 1 | `b` |
| 2 | `c` |
| 3 | `d` |

The observable result is one execution of every file across four independently schedulable actions. Each action executes its selected files serially. This follows directly from the [modulo filter](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.shard-sequencer.cjs#L44-L51).

A related boundary explains the regression test: `allFailedTests()` must not apply that filter again. With total `4`, index `1`, and the test’s nonexistent paths `[c, a, b]`, all sizes become zero. `sort()` returns `[b]`, while `allFailedTests()` returns `[a, b, c]`. Repartitioning an already selected list could silently drop files. The implementation therefore only orders that list:

```js
allFailedTests(tests) {
  return [...tests].sort(bySizeThenPath);
}
```

This method does **not** itself identify historical failures; it preserves every supplied entry. `cacheResults()` is also a no-op, so the custom sequencer does not maintain Jest’s normal timing/failure cache. See [these methods](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.shard-sequencer.cjs#L54-L60).

## 4. Tests and supporting infrastructure

**Added:** one test in [jest.shard-sequencer.test.js](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/src/jest.shard-sequencer.test.js#L1-L40). It sets total `4` and index `1`, restores the original environment afterward, and asserts both outcomes described above: ordinary sorting selects only `b`, while failed-test handling retains all three paths in order. Nonexistent paths exercise the stat-failure fallback without filesystem fixtures.

**Modified or removed tests:** none in this comparison.

**Infrastructure changes:** the shared transform becomes transpile-only, the Bazel target gains four shards and the sequencer runfile, and Jest’s cache moves under `TEST_TMPDIR` when provided. The existing `jest.setup.cjs` registration and runfile remain intact; its TextEncoder/TextDecoder polyfill is preserved, not newly introduced.

**Coverage limits:** the added test directly checks the two sequencer methods, not Jest’s complete failed-test execution path. It does not verify real-size balancing, the status-file handshake, or complete/disjoint selection across all four shards.

**Validation:** the author reports successful `bazel build //frontend:jest_test`, `bazel test //frontend:jest_test --test_output=errors`, and `checkleft run`, plus a 58-suite/449-test partition across four shards. I inspected the complete pinned comparison, supporting CI configuration, and matching installed Jest/ts-jest implementation; I did not run tests or reproduce timings.

# PR #1552: Faster Jest transforms and four Bazel-owned shards

## 1. Problem being solved

The frontend Jest target previously ran its full test list in one process using the `ts-jest` preset. The PR addresses two sources of elapsed time: TypeScript transformation overhead and serial execution of the suite. The author reports that profiling identified repeated TypeScript program construction as the dominant cost; the supplied source establishes the old configuration, but does not include those profiles. See the [base Jest configuration](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/54e4e293dfe4e142bf8a63761f4f0348af205a0e/frontend/jest.config.cjs#L1-L7) and [base Bazel target](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/54e4e293dfe4e142bf8a63761f4f0348af205a0e/frontend/BUILD#L38-L58).

This guide covers the complete comparison from `54e4e293` to `7db88ee2`. Links below pin the supplied source revisions; exact diff anchors were not provided.

## 2. Core fix / implementation

The change combines two independent optimizations:

- **Transpile files without Jest-side type checking.** An explicit `ts-jest` transform replaces the preset and enables `isolatedModules`.
- **Partition test files across four Bazel shards.** A custom sequencer reads Bazel’s runtime shard environment and selects each shard’s files. Each Jest process retains `--runInBand`, so Bazel controls parallelism.

The [transform configuration](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.config.cjs#L9-L31) contains the essential compiler settings:

```js
"^.+\\.[tj]sx?$": [
  "ts-jest",
  {
    isolatedModules: true,
    // ...
    tsconfig: {
      module: "CommonJS",
      moduleResolution: "Node",
      esModuleInterop: true,
    },
  },
],
```

The CommonJS overrides adapt the transform to Jest’s runtime. The surrounding comment says other compiler settings are inherited from the application configuration.

**Type checking is now a separate responsibility.** The PR description and configuration comment say CI runs `tsc` over all of `src`, including tests, under the same frontend-change condition. Neither that CI configuration nor the TypeScript configuration is supplied, so this retained coverage cannot be independently verified here. The Jest configuration itself does not enforce that a separate type-check runs.

## 3. Walkthrough of the implementation

### Start with the Bazel execution boundary

The [Bazel target](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/BUILD#L38-L64) still passes the globbed test paths with `--runTestsByPath` and retains `--runInBand`. It adds:

```python
"jest.shard-sequencer.cjs",  # in data
```

and:

```python
shard_count = 4,
```

Thus each shard receives the target’s test list; the sequencer performs the actual partition. Adding the `.cjs` file explicitly to runfiles matters because the existing JavaScript/TypeScript source glob does not include that extension.

### Activate the sequencer from runtime state

[Jest configuration](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.config.cjs#L3-L8) installs the custom sequencer conditionally:

```js
...(process.env.TEST_TOTAL_SHARDS
  ? { testSequencer: "<rootDir>/jest.shard-sequencer.cjs" }
  : {}),
```

The condition is a truthy environment value, not independent detection of Bazel. With that variable absent, bare Jest retains its default sequencer; the new transform still applies.

When the sequencer module loads, it [writes the shard-status file](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.shard-sequencer.cjs#L22-L25), if supplied:

```js
const statusFile = process.env.TEST_SHARD_STATUS_FILE;
if (statusFile) {
  fs.writeFileSync(statusFile, "");
}
```

This acknowledges sharding support. It happens before selection and is not validation of the shard parameters.

### Order once, then distribute by position

The [ordering helper](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.shard-sequencer.cjs#L27-L37) sorts larger files first, breaking size ties by path. Failed filesystem lookups count as size zero.

The [core partition](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.shard-sequencer.cjs#L44-L52) is:

```js
const total = Number(process.env.TEST_TOTAL_SHARDS);
const index = Number(process.env.TEST_SHARD_INDEX);
const ordered = [...tests].sort(bySizeThenPath);
if (!Number.isInteger(total) || total < 1 || !Number.isInteger(index)) {
  return ordered;
}
return ordered.filter((_, i) => i % total === index);
```

For four shards, shard zero receives positions `0, 4, 8…`; shard one receives `1, 5, 9…`. With identical ordering and valid indices, this partitions the list without overlap. File size is a cost heuristic, so equal runtime is not guaranteed.

Validation is limited: invalid totals or noninteger indices return the full ordered list, but integer indices outside `0…total-1` produce an empty selection.

### Worked example: selection and failed-test preservation

Use the [added test’s synthetic fixture](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/src/jest.shard-sequencer.test.js#L7-L10), with its [inputs and assertions](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/src/jest.shard-sequencer.test.js#L25-L38):

```text
TEST_TOTAL_SHARDS = "4"
TEST_SHARD_INDEX  = "1"
input paths: /missing/c.test.js, /missing/a.test.js, /missing/b.test.js
```

These are missing-file test objects, not executable suites.

1. **Before:** the Bazel target had no sharding, and Jest had no custom partition. There was no shard-selection step reducing the target’s test list; its default ordering is not established by the supplied code.
2. **After:** each size lookup fails and returns zero. Path ordering produces `[a, b, c]`.
3. Positions are `[0, 1, 2]`. Only position `1` satisfies `i % 4 === 1`, so `sort(tests)` returns **`[b]`**, exactly as asserted.
4. For the failed-test hook, the contract differs: an already-selected list must retain its membership. [`allFailedTests(tests)`](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.shard-sequencer.cjs#L54-L56) returns **`[a, b, c]`**. Reusing `sort()` there would incorrectly discard `a` and `c`.

The test directly proves those two method results. Jest’s caller is not supplied, so the statement that the failed-test hook receives an already-sharded list comes from the intended integration contract, rather than a traced caller. The method itself only orders its input; it does not identify failures.

### Keep temporary state scoped to Bazel

The [cache setting](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.config.cjs#L32-L34) uses `${TEST_TMPDIR}/jest-cache` when that variable is truthy; otherwise Jest chooses its default location. Separately, the custom sequencer’s [`cacheResults()` is empty](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/jest.shard-sequencer.cjs#L58-L60), so it does not persist sequencing timings.

## 4. Tests and supporting infrastructure

**Added:** one regression test asserts that `sort()` partitions the fixture while `allFailedTests()` preserves all three entries in sorted order. It sets shard variables before the test and restores their original values afterward. Missing paths exercise the zero-size fallback without creating fixture files. See the [complete test](https://github.com/brianduff/flunge/blob/7db88ee23b84dcc1a4d997bf4f29c19b5a8d66b1/frontend/src/jest.shard-sequencer.test.js#L1-L40).

**Modified or removed tests:** none in the supplied comparison.

**Infrastructure changes:** the existing Bazel glob automatically includes the new `.test.js` file; runfiles gain the sequencer; the target gains four shards; Jest gains the explicit transform, conditional sequencer, and temporary-directory cache. The existing `jest.setup.cjs` configuration and runfile entry remain present. Its claimed TextEncoder/TextDecoder polyfill is not supplied for inspection.

The regression does **not** directly test real-file size balancing, complete cross-shard coverage, status-file acknowledgement, or the separate CI type-check. Those remain distinct from the behavior its assertions establish.

The author reports successful `bazel build`, `bazel test`, and `checkleft run`, plus 58 suites and 449 tests partitioned across four shards. Reported in-band timings were 39.6–43.3 seconds versus 97.9–102.4 seconds with four Jest workers inside each shard, supporting the retained `--runInBand` choice. That comparison does not independently establish the title’s 2.2× improvement over the base revision. No tests or benchmarks were run for this guide.
